implementation_notes: Closures and function types are first-class - a step is `let normalize: (String) -> String = { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).lowercased() }` - and closure expressions, shorthand argument names and trailing-closure syntax keep steps small (docs.swift.org). The standard library ships no composition function; its compositional surface is sequence-shaped (map, compactMap, reduce), which covers element-wise transformations, so scalar chains are composed with a small generic helper or an inline closure. The helper is justified when the chain is stored or passed; a single closure wrapping two calls stays clearer for one use.
pitfalls: Closures are non-escaping by default: any step stored in a composed value must be marked @escaping, and such a closure capturing a class instance keeps it alive.
Closures capturing a struct snapshot its value, so a chain built from methods of a mutable value type keeps operating on the old copy.
@autoclosure changes evaluation timing and cannot be composed like a plain function value; keep it for call-site arguments, not chain elements.
